Credible reporting described arbitrary killing, disappearance, torture, political detention, and weak punishment of officials; nearly 700 detentions followed online protest calls, and verified videos implicated the military and army-aligned Sinai fighters in apparent executions without a reported investigation. Police also targeted LGBT people, while terrorism procedures and presidentially maintained exceptional powers exposed peaceful critics and vulnerable groups to coercion. Favorable evidence is real: Sisi reactivated a pardons committee, executions fell sharply from 2021, authorities pursued some violence against women and Copts, and insurgent activity declined. Yet releases coexisted with new arrests, death sentences increased, and reported presidential pardons of officers convicted in custodial-abuse cases would reverse rare accountability, although that beneficiary link remains leak-dependent. Sisi held formal command, security-policy, decree, and clemency authority, but the record does not prove that he ordered particular killings. This supports the severe-repression band, not the mass-terror floor; persistent abuse and deficient remedy preclude the materially higher selective-abuse
